title: Test asymmetric CCP2 next-hop rendezvous
description:
Scope: one focused CCP2 rendezvous scenario module under /home/mark/Developer/lichen-workspace/project-LICHEN/python/tests/sim/scenarios/ and minimal reuse of /home/mark/Developer/lichen-workspace/project-LICHEN/python/tests/sim/test_cross_impl_interop.py. Exercise real native-peer flows with unequal densities, sparse upper indices, receiver versus local generation, forwarded Announce origin, sender-unusable home, stale/unknown plans and CCA failures. Use independently frozen resource/observation traces as expected outcomes. No production channel-selector rewrite, mandatory hopping or RF experiment is in scope.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Keep workload and event inputs deterministic and reuse the native-peer adapter. This is an integrated behavior test, not a second rendezvous algorithm or a capacity benchmark.
acceptance_criteria: Recorded tuning and TX actions follow the authenticated actual next-hop receiver contract despite sender density/context changes. CCA failure does not retune per packet; an unusable/unknown rendezvous suppresses TX or takes only the explicitly legal control path. Sparse indices are never renumbered and remote origins are not substituted for next-hop receivers or counted as direct peers. Deterministic scenarios pass against independent expected traces across the applicable implementations.
